note: A persuasive draft judged against a lesson-facts pack: one fact is already used in the draft, the reply cites an unused one by id, and the counterargument names the other side.

assignment.title: Should students have less homework?
assignment.instructions: Write an opinion about homework. Give one reason with an example and answer the other side.

facts.text: Finland gives students about thirty minutes of homework a night.
Students who sleep nine hours remember more in class.
Short quizzes at the end of a lesson help students remember more.

sections.label: Introduction
sections.text: I think we should have less homework every night. We work hard at school all day.

sections.label: Body
sections.text: First, some countries give very little homework. In Finland students have about thirty minutes of homework a night. That gives them time to rest and play.

sections.label: Counterargument
sections.text: Some people think homework teaches us to manage our time. But I disagree because children need free time after school to play.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: For these reasons, I think we should get less homework each night.

strengths: Your opinion is clear in the first sentence.
improvements: Say how much less homework you want, like one page instead of two.
sections.evidence: I think we should have less homework every night
sections.why: A clear opinion tells the reader what you will prove.
sections.nextStep: Add one short sentence that names the amount you want.

strengths: The Finland example backs up your reason.
improvements: Explain why thirty minutes is better than more.
sections.evidence: In Finland students have about thirty minutes of homework a night
sections.why: An example is easier to trust when you say what it shows.
sections.nextStep: Add one sentence after rest and play and start it with This shows.

strengths: You name the other side and answer it in the next sentence.
improvements: Give one small detail about your time after school.
sections.evidence: Some people think homework teaches us to manage our time
sections.why: A fair answer to the other side makes your argument stronger.
sections.nextStep: Name one thing you would do with that free time.

strengths: The last sentence brings your opinion back.
improvements: Repeat your best reason in the closing sentence.
sections.evidence: I think we should get less homework each night
sections.why: A closing that repeats the main reason stays in the reader's mind.
sections.nextStep: Add because and your best reason at the end.

overall.summary: You gave a clear opinion and one country example. You also answered the other side. Next, explain how your example proves your reason.
nextPriorities: Explain the Finland example after you give it.
Add one detail about free time after school.

recommendation.reason: One sentence explaining the example will make the reason easy to follow.
